headline: Approved 2027 meeting calendar; discussed Hamden Middle School field replacement, Rochford field contract, and summer camp fees.
summary: The previous meeting's minutes were approved unanimously. Reports covered upcoming holiday events, including Hanukkah on December 8 and the tree lighting on December 9, plus a new ornament marking Hamden's 240th anniversary.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting's minutes unanimously.
Approved the 2027 meeting calendar unanimously, and kept the second Tuesday of the month at 7PM for regular meetings.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Parks & Recreation Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, November 10, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 
• Chairman Francese called the meeting to order at 7:06PM 
 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 
• In attendance: Dominic Francese, Chairman of the Parks and Recs Commission, Ryan Ott, 
Commissioner, Aryn Prestia Commissioner, Ernie Mann, Commissioner, Rick Melvin, 
Commissioner, and Karen Bivens, Director, Culture Affairs, & Human Services. 
 
 
• Absent: Rich Leonardo, Commissioner. 
 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
• The Chair motioned to approve the minutes. Commissioner Melvin seconded the motion and it 
passed with unanimously. 
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 
• No comments. 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 
• None 
 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 
• Not needed. 
 
7. REPORTS 
  
 
• Holiday planning is currently underway for Kwanza, Hanukkah (working with two local 
Rabbis), the Tree Lighting (a modified form of silver bells), the Three Kings Day, and Winter in 
the Park at Brooksvale. 
• Hanukkah will take place at the Whitney Center, where it has taken place for the past couple of 
years, and for this year it will be December 8th. 
• Tree lighting will be on December 9th. We are bringing it back to middle school, rather than 
doing it at Town Center Park (planning is underway to host activities at Memorial Town Hall, in 
the Legislative Council Chambers and will light the tree by the fountain. 
• There'll be games and activities for kids. We have been in touch with leadership from the Board 
of Ed, and we'll have some middle school and high school kids to sing ( hot cocoa will be 
served, and we will also have a visit from Santa and other special guests). 
• The Kwanzaa celebration will take place on December 20th, followed by the Three Kings on 
January 5th, both of which will be at Thornton. 
• Winter at the Park will be held at Brooksville Park. There will also be a senior center holiday 
lunch for our seniors, and that will be December 11th (more info on this can be obtained at the 
Senior Center. 
• Except the Senior Center, all other events will be free. 
• Finally, paint night will be held on December 16th. Folks can register to paint wine glasses. 
• The pool is open again after the heating system was repaired, and our regular pool schedule will 
resume on Thursday. 
• All abilities skating will take place on November 19, and Discovery Bowling will end this 
Thursday. This event will allow wheelchairs on ice for children with mobility challenges and our 
QU partners will be present to provide occupational therapy. 
• On League Stipends, we are working on issuing the stipends to the remaining leagues. 
• Karen Bevins might not be able to attend the next meeting because Hanukkah will be on the 8th. 
• Lastly, we are also doing a new ornament this year that recognizes the Town’s Hamden 240th anniversary. 
Several submissions came in from students through an art contest for which we picked the winner. Working 
closely with the Board of Ed, the ornaments will be revealed via a slide show and a website. The sale of these 
ornaments will begin in early December through the holidays. The ornaments can also be purchased on the 
Myrec site. 
•  The town’s new finance director will start in December 2026
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Hamden Middle School field replacement 
 
 
  
  
• Very expensive, and funding is going to be difficult to come up with. 
• Ryan spoke to an advocacy group with the league. Director Bivens shared that 
Representative Sweet is constantly trying to advocate for the town to get other funding for 
things. Whether the state would give us the $9.5, almost 10 that Stephen White estimated 
to do for the entire complex remains to be seen. There is also a possibility that there may 
be some, like, federally directed funding that we might have an opportunity to get 
additional funding for repairs to the library. This funding comes once a year or so. It would 
be helpful to have Rep. Rosa DeLauro be Chair of Appropriations when that time comes. 
• The Mayor continues to advocate with our legislators, including advocating to Rosa 
DeLauro, who is likely to become the chair of the Appropriations Committee. 
 
  2. Rochford field contract  
  
• An internal meeting regarding Rochford was held to figure out what it cost the town, and 
what supplies were needed. Rotchford has some major issues right now, as far as drainage, 
and issues with the membrane. 
• The Mayor will be having a meeting with the President of Albertus to discuss the current 
state of the field, and the status and viability of the existing contract. One thing to know is 
that the field has gotten worse over time. 
 
  3. League stipends 
 i. Status 
 ii. What do we want leagues to provide in 2027?  
  
• It appears all teams have requested their stipends and Director Bivens will double check if 
there is any league that has not received its stipends, but to the best of her knowledge, all 
stipends have been distributed.  
 
  4. Ice rink committee. 
• Update from Dominic and Arnie 
  
  
• Chairman Francese and Commissioner Arnie, as well as Director Bevins participated in the 
Rink Committee meeting last Thursday. 
• Director Bevins discussed various programs that the Recreation Department is involved 
with, including public skating, the All Abilities Skate, and the summer camp, skating with 
Summer Camp. Also, the Hamden Youth Hockey was there to present on their operations, 
their numbers, number of participants, especially those from Hamden.
• Is there a need to adjust the stipends in ways that could provide a little more help to 
Hockey, given how expensive that sport is? Could a tax return be asked for since the 
stipends serve more like a grant? If they could be seen as a grant, does it mean we could 
ask for financials? To be on the safe side, the Commission will consult with the Town’s 
attorney. The Commission could maybe look at how to divide it, but all leagues get the 
same amount, and the Herronets get half of it.  
• As part of the procurement process, contracts of this type can be renewed, but they 
eventually do go out to bid. Director Bevins to check on when the contract is next up for 
renewal and bidding. One thing to note is that you can't keep  giving the same contract to 
the same people. 
• Commission to closely track correspondence with the Mayor’s Office, and Director Bevins 
will continue her advocacy with the Mayor’s Office. 
 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Summer camp 
i. Fee comparison vs other towns  
  
• Commissioner Aryn put together a comparison of fees and services provided by other local 
towns. The idea was to identify different options that could be made to try to make the 
summer camp slightly closer to profitability, or closer to break-even. Below are the 
findings. 
• Except for Meriden, Hamden had the cheapest summer camp programs, and our prices 
haven’t changed since 2017, making an inflation adjustment long overdue. At the same 
time, the programs still have to consider Hamden families that would not be able to afford 
these potential new prices, while at the same time keeping in mind that new fees would 
have to be approved by the legislative council. These discussions are timely, given the 
impending arrival of our new finance director. 
 
  2. Meeting schedule 2027.  
  Voting for the 2027 Meeting Calendar: 
• Chairperson Francese made a motion to approve the new dates. Commissioner 
Rick seconded, and the motion was approved unanimously. The Commission 
voted to keep the second Tuesday of the month at 7PM as the time for its regular 
meetings.  
 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 
• The Chairperson called for a motion to adjourn at 8:51PM and the motion was seconded by 
Commissioner Rick, and passed unanimously.
